content: Project-type detection systems split into two families. (1) Per-file classification: GitHub Linguist orders strategies (modeline, filename, shebang, extension, XML header, manpage, heuristics, naive Bayes), excludes vendored/generated/documentation/data, and reports byte-weighted language stats; primary language = most bytes; manifest files are NOT used. (2) Manifest/marker-first detection: Snyk keeps an ordered DETECTABLE_FILES basename list (go.mod, package.json, pom.xml, build.gradle(.kts), packages.config, composer.lock, etc.), first existing file wins, mapped to a package manager via a basename table; langforge (Go) uses per-ecosystem detection-file lists + extension classifier with a registry; llmcli language-detect uses two phases (marker files first, extension counting fallback, 3-level depth, skip hidden dirs). Runtime managers (mise/asdf) walk up the tree for mise.toml/.tool-versions/idiomatic version files (.nvmrc, .python-version, rust-toolchain.toml, package.json, pyproject.toml) and extract only runtime versions. oh-my-zsh nvm plugin only autoloads node versions from .nvmrc via chpwd hook. Tradeoff: ordered first-match lists are simple/deterministic/low-maintenance (chosen by Snyk and the deprecated project_detector); scored/statistical approaches are heavier; plugin registries are extensible but complex. Linguist also demonstrates ignore-list hygiene (vendored/generated/docs exclusion) mirrored by our ignoreDirs list.
